newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts expect hefty Pechiney 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Analysts expect hefty Pechiney 1996 loss.

text.p: Analysts expect French aluminium and packaging group Pechiney to report hefty losses for 1996, mainly because of restructuring charges.
Sluggish aluminium and beverage can markets also should took their toll, driving operating profit down, they said.
Pechiney is due to release its full year 1996 accounts on March 6.
Pechiney, which returned to profit in 1995, the year of its privatisation, may post a net loss of 1.7 to 2.6 billion francs in 1996, analysts predicted.
"Earnings will not be good and the main unknown is the size of provisions," one analyst said.
Pechiney may write off some two to 2.5 billion francs for the Challenge restructuring plan and a patent lawsuit involving its American National Can subsidiary, analysts predicted.
Pechiney, whose sales fell four percent in 1996, may report an operating profit to 2.1-2.4 billion francs against 3.5 billion francs in 1995.
Analysts also see net income before extraordinary items ranging from a net loss of 100 million francs to a profit of 300 million francs.
Pechiney reported a 1995 net profit of 1.465 billion francs but this included 730 million francs of gains linked to asset sales.
Analysts said that it was tricky to estimate the size of 1996 provisions because the final cost to the company of the American National Can patent law suit is not yet known.
Pechiney has said that 1996 accounts are expected to reflect a $102 million (500 million francs) judgement issued against American National Can Co in a patent infringement case.
But the $102 million in damages could be increased by as much as three times since the jury deemed the infringement willful. A final ruling is still pending.
Most analysts however doubt that the final charge for the company will exceed 500 million francs.
Last month Pechiney warned that it may post a loss in the second half of 1996 but that a firmer dollar and increased world demand for aluminum would help it after the first months of 1997.
Primary aluminium prices have now rebounded to $1,600 per tonne after hitting a low of $1,400 last autumn. They reached a peak of $2,195 in Jauary 1995.
Analysts expect Pechiney to benefit from better aluminium prices in the the second half of 1997.
The company will still suffer in the first half from primary aluminium supply contracts concluded in autumn when prices were low, they said.
